regions.name: Middle East
overview: The Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia widened from the capital to the Eastern Province energy and aviation hubs. On 21 October, debris from a drone aimed at Aramco's Shaybah field killed two foreign workers, and an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one and wounded eight. Washington then ordered non-emergency embassy staff and families out of Saudi Arabia. The Houthis also struck coalition sites in Aden three times in a week, and Egypt is moving toward a parliamentary vote on 26 October on sending forces to defend Saudi territory.

The Iran–US war is at a decision point. Tanker attacks continued from the Gulf of Oman to waters off Iraq's Al-Faw, and the IRGC keeps claiming mine strikes south of Hormuz. On 20 October Iran rejected US-backed Pakistani proposals and said the strait stays closed unless its own plan is accepted. The US is sending a third carrier and about 10,000 personnel, arriving by late November. Brent rose above $110 on 22 October.

Israel is moving toward open confrontation with Iran ahead of its 27 October election. Dozens of Israeli jets flew toward Iran's border on 19 October in what Israel called a deterrence exercise, and Netanyahu said on 21 October he had instructed the IDF and Mossad to topple the Iranian government; Iran warned of a 'zero hour'. On Israel's other fronts the pattern is steady: Gaza's post-ceasefire toll passed 1,534, strikes and demolitions in south Lebanon continued as Defence Minister Katz threatened Beirut's southern suburbs, and five Israeli incursions into Quneitra and Daraa were reported on 18 October alone.

The crisis is pulling in more states and armed actors. Cairo's planned military role in Saudi Arabia drew a direct Iranian warning, and the US departure order may extend to families in Jordan, the UAE, Qatar and Bahrain. In Iraq, a blast at a PMF headquarters in Baghdad killed one member, and a tanker was hit off Al-Faw. Settler violence in the West Bank intensified in the run-up to Israel's election, including a mass attack on olive harvesters in Abu Falah on 16 October.

countries.name: Gaza
incidents: 21 Oct — Gaza Strip: The Health Ministry said 7 people were killed and 24 wounded in the previous 24 hours, raising the toll since the October 2025 ceasefire to 1,534 killed and 5,486 wounded; it warned that hospital generator fuel had run out, risking an 'immediate collapse' of equipment.
21 Oct — Gaza City: A 10-year-old boy, Abdul Rahman Khalil Awad, died of wounds from an Israeli drone strike on 19 October.

19 Oct — Khan Younis / Sheikh Radwan (Gaza City): Israeli drone strikes killed two people south of Khan Younis, including two children in the evening according to WAFA, and one person in a strike on a group in Sheikh Radwan.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Deadly Israeli strikes continue almost daily under the nominal ceasefire: the toll rose by about 40 in a week to 1,534, and children are among the dead. The collapse of hospital fuel supplies adds a severe humanitarian dimension as winter approaches. Phase two (Israeli withdrawal and Hamas disarmament) remains stalled, and Israel holds about 63% of the Strip. Over the next 90 days, expect continued targeted drone strikes in residential areas, creeping expansion of the Israeli-held zone, and worsening shortages of fuel, medicine and shelter. Little political movement is likely before a new Israeli government forms after the 27 October election. A wider Israel–Iran war would further reduce attention and aid access for Gaza.

countries.name: Lebanon
incidents: 21 Oct — South Lebanon (Kfar Tebnit, Zawtar ash-Sharqiyah, Haddatha, Wadi al-Salouqi): According to the NNA, Israel carried out a large demolition in Kfar Tebnit, a powerful blast at Ain al-Samahiyah and air strikes near Haddatha and Wadi al-Salouqi; drones flew over Tyre and Beirut, and Israeli soldiers voted in the 27 October election from positions inside south Lebanon.

20 Oct — Kfar Tibnit / Qantara / Braasheet: Israeli strikes hit Kfar Tibnit and Qantara, and a building in Braasheet was evacuated after a threatening call; Defence Minister Katz threatened to expand the occupation and strike Beirut's southern suburbs.

21 Oct — Beirut: The international conference to support the Lebanese Army was pushed to after the Israeli election; Israel ties any withdrawal from the more than 600 km² it occupies in the south to Hezbollah's disarmament, and President Aoun called for negotiations to continue.
16 Oct — South Lebanon: Israeli strikes hit several southern villages, according to L'Orient Today.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel occupies more than 600 km² of the south and carries out daily strikes and demolitions. It now openly threatens to expand the occupation and hit Beirut's southern suburbs, which would be the first such escalation since the June framework agreement. Hezbollah refuses to discuss disarmament under fire, and the army-support conference has been postponed until after the Israeli election. Over the next 90 days, the main risk is a new Israeli air campaign against the Dahiyeh or Hezbollah infrastructure, especially if Israel strikes Iran and Hezbollah responds. Expect continued civilian deaths from fire and unexploded ordnance, friction between the state and Hezbollah over seized weapons, and a widening security gap as UNIFIL's mandate ends on 31 December.

countries.name: Iran
incidents: 21–22 Oct — Hormozgan / Strait of Hormuz: A tanker was hit by an unidentified projectile about 11 nm off Bukha (Oman) and caught fire (crew safe); the IRGC Navy said a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels exploded after hitting a naval mine south of the strait, and IRNA reported several explosions of unknown cause in the Karpan area of Sirik.

20 Oct — Tehran: Iran rejected US-backed Pakistani proposals for negotiations and set conditions for talks; the foreign minister said Hormuz would stay closed unless Washington accepted Tehran's plan, and the US announced a third carrier and about 10,000 more personnel for the region.

19 Oct — Iran's western approaches: Dozens of Israeli fighter jets flew more than 800 miles toward Iran's border and turned back, which Israel called a deterrence exercise; on 22 Oct Iranian official Mohammadi warned that Iran and Israel were nearing 'zero hour'.

17 Oct — Strait of Hormuz / Gulf of Oman: The IRGC said two tankers, each carrying about 2 million barrels, caught fire after hitting mines on an 'unauthorised route' with navigation systems off; Iran's army said two more tankers burned in its 'prohibited zone' in the Gulf of Oman (none of these claims was independently verified).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. The war with the US continues. Iran is keeping up its tanker campaign, which has spread to waters off Iraq and Oman, and has rejected Pakistan's mediation, so diplomacy is stalled. The US is reinforcing with a third carrier group, Israel has rehearsed long-range strikes in plain view, and Netanyahu now openly calls for regime change. The risk of renewed strikes on Iranian territory soon after Israel's 27 October election or the 3 November US midterms is high. Over the next 90 days, expect continued attacks on shipping and mine claims at Hormuz, a probable new round of Israeli and possibly US strikes followed by Iranian missile retaliation against Israel and US bases, continued executions of January protesters, and Iranian backing for the Houthi campaign against Saudi Arabia.

countries.name: Yemen
incidents: 22 Oct — Nationwide: Yemen's government said it carried out 835 strikes on Houthi targets in 24 hours (unverified).

21 Oct — Aden / Mukalla: The Houthis said a ballistic missile struck a Saudi-led coalition operations room at Badr Camp near Aden airport, the third attack on the city in a week; Aden police told AFP that a Houthi missile caused the blast, and the Houthis also claimed a strike on coalition forces at Al Rayyan airport in Mukalla.

17 Oct — Lahij (al-Maqatirah front): Heavy clashes between government and Houthi forces killed 8 government soldiers; around the same time, government forces claimed 12 Houthi fighters killed at al-Aqroud on the edge of Taiz.
16 Oct — Aden: Two Houthi missiles landed inside the perimeter of Aden airport, the day after the strike on the al-Maashiq presidential palace.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Full-scale war continues on the Taiz, Lahij, Marib and al-Jawf fronts. Coalition air power is very active, and the Houthis keep striking Aden's leadership and coalition sites with ballistic missiles. The WHO says Taiz is functionally isolated, with hospital fuel for only four days and a growing cholera outbreak, and the IOM counts more than 233,000 displaced. Over the next 90 days, expect grinding ground battles without a decisive breakthrough, further Houthi strikes on Aden, Mukalla and Marib, and a deepening humanitarian collapse in Taiz. Egyptian forces deployed to Saudi Arabia, even in a defensive role, and possible US involvement would raise the stakes. A ceasefire is unlikely while the Houthis refuse talks.

countries.name: Israel
incidents: 21 Oct — Jerusalem: Netanyahu said he had instructed the IDF and Mossad to topple the Iranian government, calling it the only way to end the Iranian threat.
19 Oct — Northern West Bank: AP reported settler attacks in at least eight villages, with cars and olive trees set alight, as violence spiked ahead of the 27 October election.

19 Oct — Israeli Air Force: Dozens of fighter jets flew more than 800 miles toward Iran's border in what Israel told the US was a deterrence exercise; some US officials told Axios they thought Israel hoped Iran would fire on the jets.

16 Oct — West Bank (Abu Falah): Dozens of masked settlers attacked olive harvesters, set groves on fire and beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine; the Palestine Red Crescent reported about two dozen settler attacks and 20 injured that day.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No missile, rocket or drone attacks on Israeli territory were found this week. The threat inside Israel and the West Bank is recurring violence, with settler attacks surging during the harvest and ahead of the election. However, the risk of military escalation has risen sharply: the open regime-change rhetoric, the long-range flight toward Iran and Iranian 'zero hour' warnings all point to a real chance of renewed Israel–Iran hostilities in the weeks after the 27 October vote. Over the next 90 days, an Israeli strike on Iran would very likely bring Iranian missile fire and possibly Hezbollah and Houthi attacks on Israel, putting it back at CRITICAL. Expect continued West Bank violence through the harvest and the coalition talks after the election.

countries.name: Iraq
incidents: 20 Oct — Off Al-Faw (Basra): UKMTO reported that an unidentified projectile hit a tanker about 30 nm southeast of Al-Faw port (crew safe, no damage reported); an Iraqi source said the location was not confirmed as Iraqi territorial waters.
18–19 Oct — Baghdad: An explosion at a Popular Mobilisation Forces headquarters killed one PMF member and wounded four, according to security and medical sources; the cause was not disclosed.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Iraq faces recurring deadly ISIS attacks in the Kirkuk belt and unexplained blasts at militia sites, and the Iran war is reaching its southern waters. There is still no sustained armed conflict on Iraqi territory, so it does not meet CRITICAL. Over the next 90 days, the main risks are further ISIS ambushes in the disputed territories; Iraqi militias resuming drone attacks on Saudi Arabia in support of the Houthis, which would invite US or Saudi retaliation; Israeli or US strikes on PMF sites if the war with Iran resumes; and attacks on tankers near Basra that hit oil exports. Kataib Hezbollah's refusal to disarm keeps the risk of a state–militia confrontation alive.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
incidents: 21 Oct — Dammam: An attack on King Fahd International Airport killed one person and wounded eight, and operations were halted from about 23:15 local time.

21 Oct — Shaybah oil field / Eastern Province: Debris from an intercepted drone aimed at Aramco's Shaybah field killed two people, a Filipino and a Nepali national; the coalition said it intercepted six drones over the Eastern Province and Medina. On 22 Oct the US ordered non-emergency embassy staff and families to leave the kingdom.
20 Oct — Riyadh: The coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired at the capital, and witnesses heard blasts in the city.

18 Oct — Khamis Mushait / Riyadh / Eastern Province: The coalition intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Khamis Mushait and three drones over Riyadh and the Eastern Province; a Saudi AH-6i helicopter crashed near Najran, killing 2 crew (the coalition blamed a technical fault, while the Houthis claimed a shoot-down).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained and widening. Houthi missiles and drones now hit Riyadh, Khamis Mushait, Medina and the Eastern Province almost daily, with deadly strikes on a second international airport (Dammam) and on Aramco's Shaybah field. The US departure order shows that Washington expects further escalation. Over the next 90 days, expect continued salvos on airports, energy infrastructure and southern cities, more casualties from debris, prolonged aviation disruption, and pressure on foreign workers and companies to leave. External help is building: a planned Egyptian deployment (Egypt's parliament votes on 26 October), British air-defence help and possible US involvement. The Houthis have threatened the US if it joins, and a ceasefire is unlikely in the near term.

countries.name: Syria
incidents: 18 Oct — Quneitra / western Daraa: ANHA reported five Israeli ground incursions in one day, at Razaniyah, eastern Samdaniyah (checkpoint and searches), al-Ajraf (house searches), the route from the Abu al-Ghaithar gate to Ain Bahta, and Wadi al-Raqad near Jamla; further vehicles moved from the Hamidiyah base toward al-Hurriya.
18 Oct — Damascus / Daraa: Four Israeli reconnaissance aircraft flew over Damascus, and others flew over Inkhil, Nawa, Izra, al-Sanamayn and Sheikh Maskin.
20 Oct — Damascus: According to SANA, Syria strongly condemned escalating Israeli incursions into Quneitra and the Daraa countryside and urged international action.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Israel continues to hold and expand a de facto security zone in the south, with several incursions a day, checkpoints, house searches and reconnaissance flights over the capital. Damascus does not control parts of the south (the Israeli zone and Suwayda). No deadly clashes were confirmed this week, but the loss of state control and the foreign military presence have not decreased. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Israeli raids and completion of the fortified 'Sufa 53' line, a risk of Israeli strikes if government forces move south or if Syria becomes a corridor in a renewed Israel–Iran war, flare-ups in Suwayda, and continued weapons smuggling to Hezbollah. A security deal with Israel is unlikely before a new Israeli government forms.

countries.name: Egypt
incidents: 21 Oct — Cairo: President Sisi said Egypt's military support for Saudi Arabia would defend Saudi territory and borders and would not include attacking Yemen; Iranian FM Araghchi warned Egypt against intervening in Yemen.

19 Oct — Cairo: Parliament postponed its vote on authorising military support for Saudi Arabia until 26 October; a two-thirds majority is needed, and the Egyptian Social Democratic Party told its lawmakers to abstain, citing a lack of detail on objectives, duration, cost and risks.
18 Oct — Cairo: Egypt pledged 'all necessary and possible support' to Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi attacks.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed violence or terrorist attack on Egyptian territory was found this week. However, Egypt is moving toward deploying forces to Saudi Arabia, which would expose Egyptian troops to Houthi missiles and draw Iranian hostility. Over the next 90 days, the key indicators are the 26 October parliamentary vote, the size and location of any deployment, Houthi threats against Egyptian forces or Red Sea and Suez shipping, and domestic opposition to the mission. HIGH would apply if Egyptian forces or assets come under direct attack, if the Houthis target Suez-bound shipping, or if there is a significant terrorist incident in Sinai.

countries.name: Jordan
incidents: 22 Oct — Amman: A diplomatic source told AFP that US missions in Jordan, the UAE, Qatar and Bahrain would also order families to leave; the State Department said its departure order applies to Saudi Arabia only.
18 Oct — Northern and western borders: Al Jazeera reported a surge in drug smuggling from Israel into Jordan by drone and balloon, with accusations of collusion by border guards.
16 Oct — Amman: Jordan welcomed the UN Security Council's condemnation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and expressed solidarity with Riyadh; no new strike on Jordanian territory was reported.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. No attack on Jordanian territory has been confirmed since the 9 September barrage, about six weeks ago. However, the credible risk of military escalation has grown: Israel and Iran are openly preparing for renewed hostilities, Jordan hosts US forces that redeployed from Iraq, and US family departures may extend to Jordan. Over the next 90 days, an Israeli or US strike on Iran would very likely bring renewed Iranian missile and drone fire at bases in Jordan and debris over its airspace, putting it back at CRITICAL. Expect sustained high air-defence alert, continued cross-border drug and weapons smuggling by drone and balloon, and domestic sensitivity over West Bank violence.

countries.name: Libya
incidents: 16 Oct — Benghazi: Haftar's Libyan National Army showed Belarusian-made kamikaze jet drones and other new hardware at a military parade, according to Agenzia Nova.

22 Oct — New York: UNSMIL's mandate expires on 31 October, and the Security Council has yet to vote on its renewal; no new armed clashes or attacks on energy infrastructure were found for 16–22 October.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. No armed clashes or drone attacks were reported this week. The east–west divide persists, the LNA is visibly acquiring new strike drones, and the alleged link between Saddam Haftar and sabotage drone attacks in the west keeps tension high, so Libya sits at the upper end of MODERATE. Over the next 90 days, watch the UNSMIL renewal vote, renewed fighting in Zawiya and Sorman, drone attacks or blockades on oil and power infrastructure, and any east–west military build-up. Any of these on a sustained basis would justify HIGH. A return to full-scale war remains unlikely.

countries.name: Tunisia
incidents: 21 Oct — Gabes: A court sentenced ten environmental activists to up to one year in prison over a 2020 anti-pollution protest near a phosphate plant, eight of them with six-month suspended sentences, after a retrial of in-absentia convictions.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Tunisia's pattern is unchanged: judicial repression of activists, journalists and opposition figures, with no organised armed violence. The Gabes sentences show the crackdown reaching environmental protest as well as pro-Palestinian activism. Over the next 90 days, the main triggers for larger unrest are the health of the jailed Sumud Flotilla organisers, whose detention was extended, and economic frustration, including in Gabes. Expect continued prosecutions and small protests, plus secondary risk from instability and smuggling along the Libyan border.

regions.name: Ukraine/Russia
overview: Diplomacy restarted this week, on terms that largely suit Moscow. US envoy Steve Witkoff met Zelensky and European officials in Oslo on 20 October, then Putin in St Petersburg on 21 October; Jared Kushner joined by video. Russia released US prisoner Stephen Hubbard, and both Kyiv and Moscow agreed to resume trilateral talks, the first since February. A technical round on post-war security guarantees could be held in Abu Dhabi in November. The US context is still unfavourable for Kyiv: Trump put new Russia sanctions on hold (16 Oct), criticised Ukraine's refinery strikes and told Kyiv to make a deal, and the first Russian diesel tanker is heading to the US under the deal. Witkoff calling Putin a 'humanitarian' drew bipartisan criticism.

Neither side has eased strikes while talking. Ukraine flew one of its largest drone attacks of the war on 18 October; Russia's Defence Ministry reported 1,015 drones over 15 regions, and oil facilities in St Petersburg were hit. Overnight into 22 October, drones struck Lipetsk and a reported drone-and-missile attack hit the 75th Arsenal weapons plant in Serpukhov, Moscow Oblast. Russia kept up near-daily deadly strikes on Ukrainian cities, including drone and ballistic attacks on Kyiv on 19, 21 and 22 October. Zelensky said Russia used about 2,700 drones, 1,700 glide bombs and 66 missiles in a single week. Zelensky said US intelligence sharing has resumed after a pause, but Patriot interceptors remain critically short; a Lockheed Martin delegation was in Kyiv on 21 October to discuss more PAC-3 supply.

The Black Sea has become a new front against shipping. In ten days, suspected Russian drones hit at least six to seven commercial vessels off Romania and Bulgaria, with at least 23 sailors missing or dead. Moscow denies involvement and NATO has not formally attributed the attacks. On 20 October the North Atlantic Council agreed to send more maritime patrol aircraft, radars, drones and intelligence staff to the region. EU foreign policy chief Kallas called it a 'dangerous and unacceptable escalation' that threatens Ukraine's grain revenue. Elsewhere, Germany's military rated the Russian sabotage threat as 'significant' for the first time.

On the periphery there are still no hostilities, but pressure is rising. Moldova had another drone crash and explode on its soil, at Dondușeni on 16 October, plus five airspace violations in one night. Lukashenka ordered 'people's militia' units in every Belarusian village council and announced readiness inspections of the militia and territorial defence. In Georgia, the Constitutional Court began substantive hearings in Batumi (21–23 Oct) on banning five opposition parties, and an opposition rally is planned for 25 October. Azerbaijan put seven Türkiye-based critics on an international wanted list as the hijab dispute strains ties with Ankara. In Armenia, authorities arrested opposition Strong Armenia members ahead of 25 October local elections, and an EAEU report raised the prospect of suspending Armenia's membership.

countries.name: Ukraine
incidents: 22 Oct — Kyiv: An overnight Russian ballistic missile attack killed 1 person and injured 22, including 4 children. A paramedic station lost six ambulances, and damage to Kyiv Metro infrastructure on the Southern Bridge restricted cross-river traffic (Kyiv Independent).

21 Oct — Kyiv/nationwide: A drone hit a 24-storey residential building in Sviatoshynskyi district, killing 2. Across Ukraine, Russian attacks with Iskander-K cruise missiles and 186 drones killed at least 9 and injured 45 in one day, including 4 dead in Donetsk Oblast. Strikes on a gas production site in Kharkiv Oblast and infrastructure in Dnipro left about 30,000 consumers without power.

19 Oct — Kyiv/Kharkiv region/Kyiv Oblast: An overnight strike on Kyiv killed a woman, damaged a metro station and hit a 25-storey building (Al Jazeera). A Russian drone strike on a park in Kharkiv region killed 6, including 3 children, and an attack on a business in Obukhiv district killed 1 and injured 6.

18 Oct — Volyn/Zaporizhzhia: Strikes on residential buildings in Volyn killed 2 and injured 12, including 2 children. Two attacks on Zaporizhzhia killed a woman and wounded at least 2, including a six-year-old girl (Al Jazeera).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Ukraine is under full-scale attack, with deadly strikes across many regions every day, including repeated ballistic and drone attacks on Kyiv. Over the next 90 days, expect Russia to keep its winter campaign against energy and transport infrastructure going throughout any talks. Expect Black Sea drone attacks on commercial shipping to aim at Ukraine's grain-export revenue. The renewed trilateral track (Oslo, then St Petersburg, with a possible Abu Dhabi technical round in November) is the main new variable. Washington is pressing Kyiv to settle while holding sanctions on Russia and buying Russian diesel, so Kyiv faces pressure to accept a framework centred on security guarantees without a full ceasefire. Kyiv will try to keep its deep-strike campaign as leverage and will lean on Europe for financing, Storm Shadow and Danish-backed production such as the Fire Point loan. Patriot interceptor shortages remain the critical weakness, which the Lockheed PAC-3 talks will not fix in the short term. Watch for whether the Abu Dhabi talks actually happen, for any energy-truce proposal tied to them, further cuts to Starlink/Starshield, NATO escalation in the Black Sea, and the APEC sidelines, where a Trump–Putin–Xi meeting has been floated.

countries.name: Russia
incidents: 22 Oct — Serpukhov (Moscow Oblast)/Lipetsk: Witnesses told Astra that drones followed by missiles hit the 75th Arsenal weapons and ammunition plant in Serpukhov (unverified). Sobyanin said 163 drones were destroyed approaching Moscow and 2 people were injured in Voronovskoye. In Lipetsk, explosions and fires were reported and monitoring channels said a residential building was hit.

21 Oct — St Petersburg (Constantine Palace): Putin met US envoy Witkoff, released detained US citizen Stephen Hubbard and agreed to resume US-mediated trilateral talks with Ukraine, possibly in Abu Dhabi in November. The same day, the first Russian diesel tanker for the US under the Trump deal was reported, and a Su-30 crashed during training in Kaliningrad Oblast.

18 Oct — St Petersburg/Leningrad Oblast: In one of Ukraine's largest drone attacks of the war, Russia's Defence Ministry reported 1,015 drones over 15 regions. Fires broke out at the St Petersburg oil terminal, the Ruchi oil depot and Kolpinsky warehouses. One person was killed and 5 injured, and about 20,000 people lost power in Leningrad Oblast. Pulkovo airport restricted flights, and an Ozon logistics hub and a VK data centre were also hit (Al Jazeera).
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Russia is waging an active war, and its territory, from St Petersburg and the Moscow region to the border oblasts, is under drone and missile attack nearly every day, with casualties. Over the next 90 days, expect the Kremlin to use the restarted trilateral track (the Witkoff visit, the Hubbard release, possible talks in Abu Dhabi, a floated Trump–Putin–Xi meeting at APEC) to lock in Washington's sanctions hold and the diesel deal. It is unlikely to concede on territory or a full ceasefire and will keep mass strikes on Ukraine's grid going. Deniable attacks on Black Sea commercial shipping are likely to continue and could escalate friction with NATO, which is adding patrol aircraft and sensors in the region. Expect Ukraine's long-range campaign to keep hitting refineries, oil terminals, defence plants and data centres hundreds to thousands of kilometres deep. That means fuel disruption, airport closures, power outages and civilian casualties in western Russia. A Ukrainian strike that lands during the talks could be used by Moscow to drive a wedge between Kyiv and Trump. Regime stability risk remains low.

countries.name: Belarus
incidents: 16 Oct — Verkhnedvinsk district (Vitebsk region): While watching people's militia training, Lukashenka ordered militia units in every village council. He described them as the base layer under territorial defence and the army, armed with assault rifles, grenades and machine guns. He also announced a nationwide alert-and-readiness inspection of the militia and territorial defence (UNITED24, TASS).

16 Oct — Vitebsk region (Losvido range): The CSTO exercises Indestructible Brotherhood-2026 and Barrier-2026 ended on 16 October. More than 1,500 troops from five member states took part, with more than 300 pieces of equipment.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Re-tested against the definitions, Belarus has no hostilities on its own territory. Its profile remains military activity that creates tension, now including a push to militarise society down to village level and announced readiness inspections, alongside the CSTO drills and the Russian Oreshnik deployment. No new balloon or airspace incident from Belarus against Lithuania or Poland was found this week. Over the next 90 days, expect Minsk to use the militia expansion and inspections for internal control and deterrence signalling, and to keep trading prisoner releases with Washington for sanctions relief. Wall Street Journal reporting that Moscow is pressing Minsk toward deeper involvement in the war is an indicator to watch, but there is no sign that Belarusian forces will enter Ukraine. The winter season raises the risk of renewed smuggling-balloon disruption at Vilnius airport and border crossings. A rise to HIGH would require direct military coercion against NATO neighbours or a serious armed border incident.

countries.name: Moldova
incidents: 16 Oct — Dondușeni district (near Scăieni/Codrenii Noi): A drone crashed and exploded in a field. Police reported no casualties and an investigation is under way. The Foreign Ministry condemned the repeated airspace violations (Ukrainska Pravda, Logos Press).

15–16 Oct — Ștefan Vodă/Ocnița districts: During Russia's mass attack on Ukraine, the Defence Ministry recorded five drone violations in under seven hours. Entry points included Purcari, Tudora, Căplani and Otaci, and one drone left via Dnestrovsc in Transnistria. Reported totals: seven violations in 10–16 October and 63 so far in 2026 (Eurointegration, informat.ro).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. A third drone has now crashed and exploded on Moldovan soil in under three weeks (Hîrbovăț 30 Sep, Geamăna 11 Oct, Dondușeni 16 Oct), and a Russian mass attack on Ukraine now produces several violations per night. This is constant spillover, not hostilities aimed at Moldova, and there are still no casualties. Over the next 90 days, expect more incursions and debris whenever Russia strikes Odesa and Vinnytsia regions, faster purchases of EU-funded air surveillance and counter-drone systems, and continued Russian hybrid pressure. That pressure includes cyber attacks, influence operations in Gagauzia and a possible winter energy squeeze on Transnistria. Wider Black Sea attacks on shipping off neighbouring Romania raise the regional threat to Moldova's trade routes. EU accession is still stalled by Hungary's veto on opening further clusters. A first fatality from a drone, or a deliberate strike on Moldovan territory, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Georgia
incidents: 21 Oct — Batumi: The Constitutional Court opened three days of hearings (21–23 Oct) on Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban UNM, Coalition for Change, Lelo/Strong Georgia, the Federalists and For Georgia. It rejected recusal motions and refused to call Ivanishvili or Saakashvili as witnesses, and UNM's Khatia Dekanoidze was removed from the courtroom. Freedom Square protested outside and 19 civil society organisations condemned the case (Civil.ge).

21 Oct — Tbilisi: The government named First Deputy Foreign Minister Zurabashvili as the prime minister's special representative for relations with Russia, a post that had been vacant for almost a year.

20 Oct — Tbilisi: The Foreign Ministry accused EU representatives of interference after they criticised the party-ban proceedings. The Council of Europe's Secretary General called on Georgia to 'uphold political pluralism'.

19 Oct — Tbilisi: Formula TV anchor Vakho Sanaia was sentenced to 30 days' administrative detention over social media posts said to insult Speaker Papuashvili and an MP. It is his second detention for a similar offence.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There is no organised political violence and protests remain small, but the party-ban case is now in substantive hearings before a court critics consider loyal to Georgian Dream, and arrests of journalists continue. Over the next 90 days, expect a ruling that bans most or all of the five opposition forces, possibly soon after the hearings end on 23 October. Expect further administrative arrests of journalists and activists, an escalating diplomatic dispute with the EU and Council of Europe, and quiet steps toward normalisation with Moscow, such as filling the post of special representative for Russia. The 25 October 'Georgia without Ivanishvili' rally is the first test of whether mass mobilisation can return. A ban on the main opposition parties combined with large protests that are violently dispersed would justify a return to HIGH.

countries.name: Armenia
incidents: 21 Oct — Stepanavan (Lori): The Investigative Committee arrested 14 people, including Arsen Gevorgyan, the opposition Strong Armenia party's candidate for community head, on charges of giving and receiving electoral bribes ahead of the 25 October local vote. Party figures called it politically motivated (OC Media).

20 Oct — Moscow/Yerevan: A report by the Russia-led EAEU, commissioned after members asked Yerevan to choose between EU accession and the EAEU, said suspending Armenia would devastate its economy but barely affect other members. This increases Russian economic leverage (OC Media).

15 Oct — Yerevan: Pashinyan said he aims to sign and ratify the peace treaty with Azerbaijan before 2031, and floated a swap of enclaves. Baku is still demanding changes to Armenia's constitution. He also said relations with Russia had 'never' been strained.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There are no hostilities and no fatal border fire. The Shaki shooting is being handled as a criminal case, and this week's friction was political and economic, not military. Over the next 90 days, expect Moscow to step up economic coercion: possible EAEU suspension procedures with a December report deadline, trade restrictions, and unconfirmed threats to gas supply from 1 November. Pashinyan's public tone toward Moscow has softened, which suggests he is trying to avoid an open rupture. Domestically, expect the government to keep using the courts against the opposition before and after the 25 October local elections, which raises polarisation. The Azerbaijan peace track holds but is now openly long-term, with a 2031 horizon, and still blocked on the constitutional issue. Repeated armed border crossings, a deliberate shooting incident or violent post-election unrest would warrant a review toward HIGH.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
incidents: 19 Oct — Baku: The Prosecutor General's Office put seven Türkiye-based commentators, presenters, a lawyer and social media figures on an international wanted list. A Binagadi court ordered their arrest in absentia for calling for the violent seizure of power, inciting religious hatred and spreading extremist material between 25 September and 18 October (Armenpress).

17–21 Oct — Baku/Ankara: The dispute with Türkiye over the school hijab rules deepened. After criticism from Erdoğan adviser Oktay Saral, the ruling party accused Turkish officials of interference, and the Foreign Ministry added 31 Turkish citizens, mostly religious and media figures, to its list of undesirable persons. TikTok was restricted in schools. Iran said Azerbaijanis 'should resolve' the issue with their government (OC Media, Euronews TR).
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There are no hostilities on Azerbaijani territory. The hijab protests are among the largest in years but have produced detentions, internet restrictions and prosecutions, not lethal violence. Over the next 90 days, expect Baku to keep framing the protests as foreign-driven religious extremism, with more in-absentia charges, entry bans, arrests of activists and online restrictions such as the planned social-media ban for under-16s. The most notable new risk is a rift with Türkiye, Baku's main ally, alongside Iranian media amplification and closer ties with Israel. With Armenia, the peace track is slow but intact, and the Shaki soldier case is being treated as a criminal matter. Violent clashes during the protests, or a pattern of armed incidents with Armenia or Iran, would warrant a review toward HIGH.

regions.name: Sahel
overview: Sudan's war has entered a phase of mass-casualty drone warfare against civilian targets on both sides: on 18–19 October drone strikes hit a transport hub near a market in al-Dabab (West Kordofan), killing 80 to 150 people, and the Amiet market in the disputed Abyei area, where local authorities blamed a Sudanese army strike for 53 to more than 150 deaths. South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador over the Abyei strike, giving the conflict a new cross-border dimension. RSF drone strikes on eastern Khartoum and army strikes on Nyala show that no city is outside the war, while the threatened RSF assault on El Obeid is still pending.

In north-east Nigeria ISWAP and Boko Haram pressure on the army is at its highest level of the year: more figures emerged on the 13 October Mairari base overrun (about 15 soldiers and 5 CJTF killed), and on 17 October a mine-and-ambush attack on a patrol on the Gamboru Ngala–Cameroon road killed about 10 soldiers and 5 CJTF members. Three costly attacks on army positions in under two weeks point to a dry-season offensive around Lake Chad.

In the central Sahel the Islamic State is retaliating against civilians: on 18 October IS gunmen on motorbikes killed about 40 to 50 mostly Tuareg (Idaksahak) civilians at Tagadayat near Ménaka in Mali, apparently in retaliation for FAMa/Africa Corps operations against the group. On 19 October Human Rights Watch documented abuses by the Malian army and Africa Corps against civilians, and executions of captured soldiers by jihadists, since July. Burkina Faso's junta reinstated the death penalty for terrorism, treason and espionage on 21 October, a further sign of repression amid the insurgency.

Information gaps persist: no independently verified attack in Niger and none on state forces in Burkina Faso was found for 15–22 October, which reflects junta information blackouts rather than calm. Chad saw new internal violence, with 12 killed in a farmer–herder clash in Salamat on 18 October and arrests over a 14 October attack on a mining-brigade post at Miski (Tibesti). All threat levels are unchanged: Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso, Sudan and Nigeria CRITICAL, Chad HIGH, Mauritania MODERATE.

countries.name: Mali
incidents: 19 Oct — Central and northern Mali: Human Rights Watch reported that since July FAMa and Russia's Africa Corps have killed and wounded dozens of civilians in counter-insurgency operations, while Islamist and separatist fighters have tortured and executed captured Malian soldiers.

18 Oct — Tagadayat, near Ménaka: Gunmen on motorbikes attributed to the Islamic State killed about 40 to 50 mostly Tuareg (Idaksahak) civilians, 48 according to the community's executive bureau; an attack on a community leader's residence in Ménaka the same day was repelled. Witnesses described it as retaliation for a recent FAMa operation against the group.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: JNIM, the FLA and the Islamic State all hold territory and carry out regular deadly attacks on state forces, militias and civilians. Over the next 90 days FAMa and the Africa Corps will likely push north from Kidal toward Aguelhok, Tessalit and Tinzaouatène and keep striking IS Sahel in Ménaka, which is likely to trigger more IS reprisals against Tuareg and Daoussahak communities that it sees as collaborating with the state. JNIM remains the main threat to the state, through garrison assaults in central and western Mali, IEDs around Mopti/Sévaré and its fuel blockade on the Senegal and Sikasso corridors. Documented abuses by the army and Africa Corps will feed recruitment and displacement toward Mauritania, Algeria and Niger, and heavy losses keep the risk of discontent inside the military elevated.

countries.name: Niger
incidents: 15–22 Oct — Nationwide: No independently verified, dated attack was found for this window; the junta's restrictions on reporting mean this is an information gap, not a lull.

26 Sep — Birni-N'Konni area, Tahoua region: Most recent major reported incident: An ISSP attack killed more than 30 soldiers, days after an ambush on a gendarme convoy near Abala–Filingué (Tillabéri); ISSP claimed both, with combined security-force losses above 50.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: the threat has not decreased. ISSP mass-casualty attacks in late September, the August Niamey mutiny and the continuing purge of the army point to sustained insurgency and acute regime instability, and a second week without reporting does not mean the threat has fallen. Over the next 90 days ISSP ambushes on army and gendarmerie convoys in Tillabéri and attacks along the Tahoua–Dosso belt toward Nigeria are likely to continue, along with IS reprisals against civilians on the Ménaka border similar to Tagadayat in Mali. JNIM pressure in the south-west toward Benin is also likely. The junta will put regime protection first, relying on the Africa Corps and arrests of officers and critics, which keeps morale low and makes another coup or mutiny attempt a realistic possibility. Casualty figures will keep surfacing late, through ISSP claims and anonymous sources.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
incidents: 21 Oct — Ouagadougou: The transitional legislature unanimously (71–0) approved a revised penal code that reinstates the death penalty for terrorism, treason and espionage, abolished in 2018, giving the junta a new legal tool against perceived threats.

16 Oct — Oudalan province: Further reporting on IS Sahel's claim to have killed more than 400 JNIM fighters at Ganadaouri; the journalist collective Wamaps said the fighting in the tri-border area began on 9 Oct. The figure remains unverified.
15–22 Oct — Nationwide: No independently verified attack on army or VDP positions was found, in line with the junta's continuing information blackout.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: two jihadist groups fight the state and each other across much of the country, and the absence of reported attacks reflects the blackout, not calm. Over the next 90 days the JNIM–IS Sahel contest for Oudalan and Liptako-Gourma will likely keep producing high-casualty clashes, while JNIM keeps overrunning army and VDP posts in the North, East and Boucle du Mouhoun and keeps up the sieges of Djibo, Sebba and Titao. Large garrison assaults are likely as the dry season sets in. The death-penalty law points to tighter repression of dissent and suspected collaborators, and could be used against officers accused of plotting. Analysts should rely on group claims, displacement data and cross-border reporting, and watch for instability inside the junta.

countries.name: Sudan
incidents: 19 Oct — Amiet market, Abyei: Local authorities said a Sudanese army drone strike using 22 munitions killed at least 53 people and wounded 27, and later reports put the toll above 150; an army officer said fuel tankers bound for the RSF were targeted. South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador.

19 Oct — Khartoum and Nyala: Drone strikes killed four people, including three children, at two sites in eastern Khartoum, attributed to the RSF, while the army struck RSF positions in Nyala (South Darfur) and West Kordofan. Emergency Lawyers said drone attacks killed more than 160 people across Sudan over several days.

18 Oct — al-Dabab, West Kordofan: A double drone strike on a transport hub near a market, including a truck carrying mourners and a funeral tent, killed 80 according to residents and medics and up to 150 in later counts. The RSF-led Tasis administration blamed the army, and the Sudan War Observatory said the drones may have been launched from Kadugli.
17 Oct — West Kordofan: A Sudanese army drone strike killed four civilians, according to Sudan Tribune.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: full-scale war continues on several fronts, with mass-casualty drone strikes by both sides on markets and transport hubs. Over the next 90 days the RSF is likely to attempt a siege or assault on El Obeid, cutting power, water and fuel, while SAF builds on its al-Mazroub gain and widens its drone campaign against RSF supply lines in West Kordofan and Darfur. The Abyei strike shows that this campaign now reaches across contested borders and risks a diplomatic crisis with South Sudan, while Blue Nile and the alleged launches from Ethiopia keep an eastern cross-border front open. With al-Burhan rejecting talks, a truce is unlikely. Expect continued high civilian casualties, new displacement into Chad and South Sudan, and deepening famine.

countries.name: Chad
incidents: 21 Oct — N'Djamena: Prosecutors charged four suspects with murder, undermining state integrity and criminal association over the 14 Oct attack on a mining-brigade position at Miski, Tibesti; security forces displayed ten seized weapons, including two bazookas. On 20 Oct the opposition coalition COSADT called for a ceasefire and dialogue in the Tibesti.

18 Oct — Kouzi-Wahit, Bahr-Azoum department, Salamat: A clash between farmers and Arab herders over a transhumance route killed at least 12 people and wounded many; the army was deployed, and on 20 Oct provincial authorities arrived with reinforcements to restore calm.
14 Oct — N'Djamena/Paris: France and Chad signed a letter of intent to restore defence cooperation on a new basis.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained: Chad faces recurring armed violence, including Boko Haram around Lake Chad (state of emergency since May), renewed armed tension in the gold-mining north (Miski/Tibesti) and deadly intercommunal clashes in the south-east, but there are no ongoing hostilities with regular deaths on a CRITICAL scale. Over the next 90 days the dry-season transhumance will likely bring more farmer–herder violence in Salamat, Ouaddaï and Moyen-Chari, while the Tibesti gold conflict may escalate if Miski self-defence groups resist government control. A likely RSF push on El Obeid and drone warfare in Darfur will keep refugee arrivals at Tiné and Adré high, and a repeat of the March or August cross-border strikes would justify CRITICAL. Renewed defence ties with France and the link with Haftar show Déby diversifying his security partners.

countries.name: Mauritania
incidents: 15–22 Oct — Nationwide: No significant new security incident on Mauritanian territory was found in this window.

8 Oct — Hodh Chargui/Mali border: MSF reported that wounded civilians regularly cross from central and northern Mali for treatment, that a drone hit a camp about 20 km from the border in mid-September, and that many refugees live outside Mbera camp in informal sites with little water or healthcare.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained: Mauritania has no organised armed violence on its own territory; its risk comes from border friction with Mali, refugee pressure and migration. Over the next 90 days FAMa and Africa Corps operations in the north and centre of Mali, documented by HRW on 19 Oct, together with JNIM activity in western Mali, are likely to push more refugees into Hodh Chargui and raise the risk of drone or ground incidents involving Mauritanian herders near the border, keeping relations with Bamako tense. Nouakchott will likely stick to containment through diplomatic protests and precautionary measures. Migrant interdictions on the Atlantic route will keep drawing human-rights criticism. A JNIM attack inside Mauritania or an armed border clash would justify HIGH.

countries.name: Nigeria
incidents: 17 Oct — Gamboru Ngala–Cameroon border road, Borno: A patrol from the Gamboru battalion hit a landmine, likely planted by Boko Haram, and came under fire; about 10 soldiers and 5 CJTF members were killed, according to soldiers who spoke to Reuters (AFP sources put army deaths at eight). No official statement was issued.

15–16 Oct — Mairari, Guzamala LGA, Borno: Fuller accounts of the 13 Oct ISWAP overrun of the military base put the toll at about 15 soldiers and 5 CJTF killed, with several soldiers missing and the base destroyed and looted; the military has still not issued an official toll.

12–13 Oct — Bukkuyum LGA, Zamfara: A military source confirmed that bandits ambushed an army-escorted traders' convoy, killing at least 20 people, including four soldiers, three police officers and an NSCDC officer, and wounding 19.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained: three costly ISWAP or Boko Haram attacks on army positions and patrols in Borno within two weeks (Kukawa 6–7 Oct, Mairari 13 Oct, Gamboru 17 Oct), plus deadly bandit attacks on escorted convoys and military camps in Zamfara, confirm a sustained insurgency with regular military deaths. Over the next 90 days ISWAP is likely to keep up night raids on isolated forward bases in Guzamala, Kukawa, Marte and Abadam as the dry season improves mobility, and IED and ambush attacks on main supply routes toward the Cameroon border, with the military relying on airstrikes of uncertain effect. In the north-west, bandit attacks on camps, mining sites and convoys in Zamfara, Katsina and Sokoto will continue, and killings in Plateau's Bokkos area risk reprisals. These security failures will add to political pressure ahead of the election cycle.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
overview: The Korean peninsula has moved from a missile test-for-test cycle to direct friction on the land border. On 19–22 October Kim Yo Jong announced that new 'firepower units' had taken up firing positions along the DMZ and said propaganda loudspeakers would be running along the entire border within days. She threatened to 'mercilessly eliminate' South Korean forces if warning fire harmed the North. Seoul ordered a firmer DMZ posture after repeated North Korean crossings of the Military Demarcation Line were met with warning broadcasts and shots; these are the highest inter-Korean tensions since President Lee took office in 2025.

Pakistan's two-front crisis continues. Pakistani and Afghan Taliban forces exchanged fire for about four hours in Kurram and Paktia on 17 October after a TTP infiltration attempt. Militants also kept up attacks on police and troops, including a police post in Peshawar on 15 October and an IED that killed an army major in Gwadar on 18 October. Governor's rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa now faces seven constitutional petitions in the Peshawar High Court, and the PTI says its protest march continues.

Japan and the US opened Keen Sword 27 on 19 October, their largest edition yet, with about 45,000 Japanese and 11,000 US personnel and seven partner nations. China answered with surveillance. On the opening day two PLA drones and a Y-9 intelligence aircraft flew through the Okinawa–Miyako gap, the first confirmed drone passage there since June 2025, and a PLAN intelligence ship transited the Osumi Strait. Around Taiwan, 13 PLA aircraft crossed the median line on 14–15 October as the Liaoning group deployed, and Taipei is preparing for a possible large-scale drill in the November–December season. In the South China Sea, the PLA shadowed USS Charleston near Sabina Shoal on 20 October. Manila summoned China's ambassador on 19 October over his remark that China could 'easily win' a war.

Myanmar's air war is still intense. AAPP verified 65 deaths from junta airstrikes between 1 and 20 October, and a strike in Yesagyo (Magway) on 16 October reportedly killed 11–15 civilians. In Rakhine, the junta's counteroffensive at Nga Pyi Island outside Sittwe is stalling, and the Arakan Army has damaged a third navy vessel. Elsewhere, violence was lethal but local: a Kuki-Meitei flare-up around Imphal killed four on 18–19 October, an infiltration attempt in Kupwara was stopped on 17 October, and six people died in Thailand's Deep South on 16–17 October.

countries.name: North Korea
incidents: 21–22 Oct — DMZ (via KCNA): After touring frontline fortification sites with military officials on 20 Oct, Kim Yo Jong said anti-South loudspeakers would be on standby along the entire border within days and running by the end of October. She warned of 'the most horrible and distressing situation' and said troops would 'mercilessly eliminate' South Korean forces if their warning fire harmed North Korean territory or personnel.

20 Oct — Inter-Korean border: Kim Yo Jong said new firepower units had 'taken their firing positions' on the border, a day after threatening to deploy more tactical strike assets. North Korean border troops were reportedly ordered to take 'resolute action' if their safety was threatened.

21 Oct — Pyongyang: North Korea again rejected the ROK–UN Command finding that its mines caused the 21 Sep DMZ blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers, calling it an 'absurd assertion' meant to shift blame.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect Pyongyang to turn its border fortification campaign into active pressure: loudspeakers back on, new artillery and tactical strike units forward-deployed, and continued crossings of the MDL by work and security parties. Each crossing risks warning fire from the South, which Pyongyang has now said it will answer with force. This is the most likely path to a kinetic exchange, more likely than missile testing. Further ballistic and hypersonic launches remain likely around the end of Keen Sword (29 Oct) and any allied drills. A nuclear test remains a low-probability, high-impact wildcard.

countries.name: Myanmar
incidents: 18 Oct — Nga Pyi Island, Pauktaw Township, Rakhine State: Arakan Army artillery reportedly hit another navy vessel off the island, the third damaged in recent days, as the junta's landing operation to break the AA blockade of the Kaladan corridor and shield the Shwe Mingan naval base in Sittwe suffered further setbacks. Estimates of regime losses range from a dozen (Irrawaddy) to at least 50 killed (DVB).

18 Oct — Paletwa Township, Chin State: Junta aircraft reportedly dropped close to 20 bombs around a motorboat jetty near Chaung Sone village, killing and injuring several civilians, including an infant.

16 Oct — Yesagyo Township, Magway Region: An airstrike on a PDF-controlled village destroyed roadside houses and an internet shop. A PDF member and witnesses said 11 people were killed, including six women and two children; Khit Thit Media reported 15 dead.

20 Oct — Nationwide: AAPP verified 65 deaths from junta airstrikes between 1 and 20 Oct, including nine children, with Rakhine (20), Magway (19) and Sagaing (14) worst hit; 42 further reported deaths are still unverified. Separate strikes on villages in Bilin (Mon) and Kyainseikgyi (Karen) townships reportedly killed at least eight civilians in mid-October.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Over the next 90 days, the Arakan Army is likely to hold its blockade around Sittwe and keep up pressure on Kyaukphyu. The junta's amphibious push at Nga Pyi has so far cost it vessels and troops without breaking the siege. The military will lean even harder on air power. With roughly three civilian airstrike deaths a day in October, expect mass-casualty strikes to continue in Rakhine, Magway, Sagaing, Chin and the southeast. Any loss of the Sittwe naval base or of Kyaukphyu would be a strategic turning point and would draw more Chinese involvement. No negotiated de-escalation is in sight.

countries.name: Pakistan
incidents: 18 Oct — Gwadar and Kalat, Balochistan: Army Major Wajahat Waheed was killed by an IED during a clearance operation in Shadi Kaur, Gwadar. The ISPR said four militants were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Jattakabad, Kalat, and eight more 'India-backed' militants were reported killed in separate operations in the province.

17 Oct — Kurram district, KP / Paktia, Afghanistan: After a TTP infiltration attempt, Pakistani troops and Afghan Taliban forces exchanged artillery and small-arms fire for about four hours at several points along the border. Pakistan said it destroyed Taliban posts and killed militants; Afghan media claimed seven Pakistani soldiers were killed. Neither claim is verified.

15 Oct — Hassan Khel, Peshawar: Militants attacked the Spina Mela police checkpost overnight, killing Constable Muhammad Jalal before withdrawing under return fire. It was the latest in a run of attacks on KP police, including the killing of an SHO and his guard near Karak on 8 Oct.

13–20 Oct — Peshawar: The Peshawar High Court issued notices to the federal government on PTI petitions against the emergency and governor's rule in KP, and a two-member bench took up seven constitutional petitions. The government says the arrangement will initially last six months, and the PTI says its long march continues.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect intermittent artillery duels and infiltration fights along the Kurram–Paktia and wider Durand Line front, with a risk of renewed Pakistani air strikes in Afghanistan. Diplomatic calls for de-escalation from Russia and the EU have produced no talks. Attacks by the TTP and its affiliates on KP police posts will likely continue at the record pace of September (225 nationwide attacks, per PICSS). BLA/BLF IED and ambush activity in Balochistan, including the Gwadar coast, will keep causing military casualties. Governor's rule and the PHC litigation will keep PTI street mobilisation going and divert security forces, which risks further violent protests.

countries.name: India
incidents: 18–19 Oct — Imphal West and Imphal East, Manipur: Four people were killed in two incidents. Suspected Kuki militants shot dead three Meitei villagers collecting firewood at Khamenlok, near the Kangpokpi boundary, and wounded three others. Separately, a 24-year-old man died of gunshot wounds after stone-pelting and firing at a music event. Police used tear gas and lathi charges on residents who carried bodies to the Chief Minister's residence, and an MLA demanded the removal of a nearby Suspension of Operations camp.

17 Oct — Jumgund, Keran sector, Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir: Troops foiled an infiltration attempt across the Line of Control. The Army said two infiltrators were killed and their bodies lay on the Pakistani side, and a search operation followed.

9–10 Oct — Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul, Manipur: Kuki–Naga clashes killed nine to ten people. Kuki–Naga violence alone had already killed at least 36 people in 2026, and the state now has active Kuki–Naga and Kuki–Meitei flashpoints.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, Manipur is likely to see more reprisal killings, including along the Imphal valley–Kangpokpi foothills where Kuki–Meitei violence has flared again, alongside the Kuki–Naga conflict in the hill districts. Expect protests targeting the SoO camps, blockades and intermittent curfews. In Jammu and Kashmir, infiltration attempts in Kupwara, Poonch and Rajouri will peak before winter closes the passes. India–Pakistan tension remains a background factor, but no direct military incident has been reported.

countries.name: China
incidents: 20 Oct — Sabina Shoal, Spratlys: The PLA Southern Theater Command said the US littoral combat ship USS Charleston 'illegally intruded' into waters next to the shoal, and that it sent naval forces to track and monitor it. It was the first publicly known US freedom-of-navigation-style transit in the South China Sea in over a year.

19 Oct — Okinawa–Miyako gap / Osumi Strait: On the opening day of Keen Sword, PLA BZK-005 and TB-001 drones and a Y-9 intelligence aircraft flew between Okinawa and Miyakojima into the Pacific and back, prompting JASDF scrambles. A PLAN intelligence-collection ship (hull 798) transited the Osumi Strait, and state media called the exercise and Japan's Type-25 missile deployment a 'clear provocation'.

15–19 Oct — Manila/Beijing: Ambassador Jing Quan said on 15 Oct that China could 'easily win' a conflict with the Philippines but would not use force. Manila summoned him on 19 Oct, and the Chinese Foreign Ministry told Manila to 'restrain' politicians calling for his expulsion.

14–15 Oct — Western Pacific / Taiwan Strait: As the Liaoning carrier group began 'routine' western Pacific drills, Taiwan detected 15 PLA aircraft, 10 PLAN ships and 7 official ships overnight, with 13 aircraft crossing the median line.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Over the next 90 days, Beijing is likely to keep stepping up activity after the summit lull. Expect close ISR shadowing of Keen Sword and allied forces through the Ryukyu gaps, more median-line crossings, and a meaningful chance of a large named drill around Taiwan during the November–December peak training season; the PLA has held none in 2026 so far. Coast guard and militia pressure on the Philippines, and on Japan around the Senkakus, will continue, alongside sharper diplomatic signalling such as the 'easily win' remark. China's own territory faces no armed threat and internal security is stable. The main risk is a collision or confrontation involving its own forces at sea or in the air.

countries.name: Taiwan
incidents: 19 Oct — Around Taiwan: The MND detected 5 PLA aircraft sorties, three of which crossed the median line, along with 6 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships.

18 Oct — Around Taiwan: The MND detected 2 PLA aircraft sorties, both crossing the median line, along with 5 PLAN vessels and 9 official ships. The higher number of official (coast guard) ships continues the 'law enforcement' trend seen since the summer.

15 Oct — Taipei: Deputy Chief of the General Staff for Intelligence Pan Chun-kuang said the MND was closely watching for a possible large-scale PLA exercise as the November–December peak drill season approaches; there has been none in 2026 so far.

14–15 Oct — Taiwan Strait: In the 12 hours to 06:00 on 15 Oct, 15 PLA aircraft, 10 naval ships and 7 official ships operated around Taiwan, with 13 aircraft crossing the median line into the northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ. Taiwan deployed patrol aircraft, navy ships and coastal missile systems.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect regular median-line crossings, a steady naval presence and a growing number of China Coast Guard and other official ships around the island and its outlying islands. The November–December window is the most likely time for a named large-scale encirclement exercise, especially if Washington moves on the paused $14 billion arms package or Taipei takes steps Beijing considers provocative. Taipei will keep pushing higher defence spending and asymmetric programmes.

countries.name: Philippines
incidents: 20 Oct — Sabina (Escoda) Shoal, Spratlys: The PLA tracked and monitored USS Charleston near the shoal, which lies in the Philippine EEZ, and accused it of 'illegal intrusion'. The AFP spokesperson said the US ship did not trespass into any Chinese territory.

19 Oct — Manila: The DFA summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan over his 15 Oct remark that China could 'easily win' a military conflict with the Philippines. Foreign Secretary Lazaro called the remark 'provocative and unacceptable' and said it conveyed a threat of force. Senators Ejercito and Pangilinan and House members called for his recall or a persona non grata declaration.
19–22 Oct — Japan: Philippine forces are taking part in Keen Sword 27 with Japan, the US and other partners. Chinese state media has framed the drills as aimed at China.

15 Oct — Lawak (Nanshan) Island, Spratlys: The PCG chased away a Chinese fishing vessel and four smaller boats launched from a mother ship, citing violations of the Fisheries Code and the Maritime Zones Act.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect continued China Coast Guard blocking, water-cannon use and ramming at Scarborough Shoal, Second Thomas Shoal and Pag-asa. These follow the 8 Oct water-cannon attack on a medevac mission and the 11 Oct militia collision with BRP Datu Cabaylo. Expect PLA air intercepts and militia swarming in the Kalayaan islands, and possibly more US transits near Sabina Shoal. The diplomatic row over Ambassador Jing could escalate if Manila expels him. A fatal incident or a serious collision would raise the risk of Mutual Defense Treaty consultations. Mindanao and NPA violence on land remains low-level.

countries.name: South Korea
incidents: 22 Oct — Seoul: The Unification Ministry urged Pyongyang to stop 'actions that violate the Armistice Agreement' and to agree on the MDL and a communication channel, repeating its offer of military talks, after Kim Yo Jong said loudspeakers would be ready within days.

20–21 Oct — DMZ, eastern front: The JCS said North Korean troops had crossed the MDL dozens of times over three days during fortification work. South Korean forces answered with warning broadcasts and warning shots, which the MND called 'legitimate and defensive measures'. Seoul said it would respond decisively if Pyongyang used them as a pretext for provocation.

20 Oct — Seoul: JCS Chairman Jin Yong-sung ordered frontline units to strengthen their operational posture in the DMZ and respond firmly to provocations. Seoul voiced 'grave concerns' over the North's plan to deploy additional strike assets on the border and pledged to strengthen control of the DMZ.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, the main risk shifts from missile tit-for-tat to the DMZ itself. Repeated MDL crossings, South Korean warning fire, newly deployed North Korean firepower units and the return of loudspeakers create a real chance of an armed exchange on the border. President Lee's engagement policy is caught between de-escalating and deterring, and domestic pressure to respond firmly is growing. Watch for live fire across the MDL, mine or drone incidents, a South Korean decision on its own loudspeakers, and North Korean reactions to the end of Keen Sword.

countries.name: Vietnam
incidents: 20 Oct — Sabina Shoal, Spratlys: The PLA shadowed USS Charleston near Sabina Shoal, a feature in the Spratly group that Vietnam also claims. Hanoi made no public reaction, and no Vietnam–China maritime incident was reported between 15 and 22 Oct.

12 Oct — Laos/Cambodia: Analyses published in Vietnam describe Chinese military footprints on both of its western flanks: Ream naval base in Cambodia and an air facility in Laos. This adds to Hanoi's concerns as it continues defence talks with Vientiane.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Over the next 90 days, Vietnam is likely to continue its two-track policy: high-level political engagement with Beijing alongside formal protests over the Paracels build-up at Antelope Reef and Yagong Island, and continued fortification of its own Spratly features. Watch for Chinese pressure on Vietnamese fishermen in the Paracels, Chinese reactions to Vietnam's Spratly runway, and stronger security cooperation with Laos and Cambodia in response to China's presence there. A direct naval confrontation remains unlikely.

countries.name: Japan
incidents: 19 Oct — Okinawa–Miyakojima gap: On Keen Sword's opening day, the JASDF scrambled fighters after a Chinese BZK-005 drone and a Y-9 intelligence aircraft flew from the East China Sea through the gap into the Pacific and back. A TB-001 drone entered the Pacific between Taiwan and Yonaguni, flew as far as Amami Oshima and returned through the same gap. Defence Minister Koizumi said it was the first confirmed Chinese drone passage there since June 2025.
19 Oct — Osumi Strait: Japan tracked the Chinese navy intelligence-collection ship hull 798 as it transited toward the Pacific during the exercise.

19–29 Oct — Southwestern islands: Keen Sword 27 began. About 45,000 Japanese personnel, 6,100 vehicles, 40 ships and 260 aircraft are taking part alongside about 11,000 US troops and forces from Australia, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, New Zealand and the Philippines. Beijing condemned the deployment of the Type-25 missile to training grounds.

14–15 Oct — South of Ishigaki: Koizumi said the Liaoning carrier group's flight operations about 250 km south of Ishigaki showed that Japan's surveillance on the Pacific side is 'limited' and that strengthening it is urgent.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained; watch for upgrade. Over the next 90 days, expect continued Chinese drone, ISR-aircraft and intelligence-ship activity through the Ryukyu gaps during and after Keen Sword, possible Chinese–Russian joint bomber patrols, and steady China Coast Guard pressure around the Senkakus. North Korea's longer-range tests keep a risk of overflights or impacts inside Japan's EEZ. A close-quarters air or maritime incident, a radar lock-on, or a missile landing in the EEZ would justify an upgrade to HIGH.

countries.name: Indonesia
incidents: 19 Oct — Gome District, Puncak, Central Papua: The Damai Cartenz task force arrested a wanted suspect, identified as PW, over a 2021 arson attack on a company camp attributed to an armed group.

17 Oct — Intan Jaya, Central Papua: The Damai Cartenz task force raided and destroyed a forest hideout it attributed to the TPNPB Kodap VIII Soanggama group, recovering 559 spent 5.56 mm cartridges, rifle parts, a Morning Star flag and TPNPB documents.

16 Oct — Maybrat, Southwest Papua: Habema operations command troops recovered from a cave a rifle and 17 rounds that had been seized by OPM fighters. This followed the 9 Oct firefight in which the TNI said three OPM members were killed, including suspected Sorong Raya commander Manfred Fatem.

12 Oct — Dekai, Yahukimo, Highland Papua: Reported 15 Oct: The TPNPB claimed it executed four people it called security or intelligence personnel. The Cartenz task force said two people were killed and both were civilians.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect TPNPB killings of non-Papuan civilians, drivers and people it labels informants, especially along the Trans-Papua highway and in Yahukimo, Jayawijaya and Intan Jaya. TNI and Cartenz operations will continue, with lethal firefights, raids on camps, arrests and disputed casualty claims, mainly in Maybrat, Intan Jaya and Puncak. Allegations of extrajudicial killings and new displacement will follow. Jakarta shows no sign of opening dialogue, so deadly violence is likely to continue weekly or fortnightly.

countries.name: Thailand
incidents: 19 Oct — Bangkok: After the second closed UNCLOS conciliation round with Cambodia in The Hague (15–18 Oct), Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said Thailand remains committed to settling the maritime dispute in the Gulf of Thailand through bilateral dialogue.

17 Oct — Ban Tueng Ngo, Sri Sakhon district, Narathiwat: A joint police and military raid on a suspected insurgent hideout led to a gun battle lasting more than ten minutes. Police Sergeant Saroj Hodnuan and three suspected insurgents were killed, two rangers of the 49th Ranger Task Force were seriously wounded, and two M16 rifles were recovered.
16 Oct — Mai Kaen district, Pattani: Gunmen ambushed territorial defence volunteer Rusli Uma as he rode to Friday prayers. He was killed, but his return fire killed one attacker.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Over the next 90 days, the Thai–Cambodian land ceasefire is likely to hold, and the maritime dispute will move slowly through conciliation and bilateral talks. Local trench and landmine disputes keep a small risk of shooting incidents. In the Deep South, the 16–17 Oct deaths show the BRN-linked insurgency remains lethal but confined to one area: expect intermittent ambushes, raids and bombings around the delayed peace talks, which are expected in late October without a confirmed Malaysian mediator. A sustained wave of coordinated mass-casualty attacks would warrant reassessment.

countries.name: Bangladesh
incidents: 20 Oct — Dhaka: Jamaat-e-Islami's secretary general held an emergency press conference accusing the BNP government of authoritarian practices, ignoring opposition demands and 'paving the way' for the Awami League's return. This came after the government signalled on 6 Oct that it was open to conditional reconciliation with the banned party.

19 Oct — Dhaka: The Human Rights Support Society reported 73 deaths and 6,473 injuries in 1,013 incidents of political violence in January–September 2026, mostly BNP infighting or inter-party clashes. It also recorded 187 deaths from mob violence, 95 deaths in prison custody and 12 deaths in law-enforcement custody.
15 Oct — Gazipur: An Awami League leader died after falling ill in custody at Gazipur District Jail; the party demanded an independent investigation into the custodial deaths of its members.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Over the next 90 days, expect continued low-level but deadly political violence, driven by BNP factional rivalry, sharper BNP–Jamaat polarisation over the Awami League question, and sporadic Awami League flash protests met by arrests. High rates of mob violence and custodial deaths point to weak rule of law rather than organised armed conflict. An upgrade would be warranted if ICT death sentences are carried out, if moves on Awami League reconciliation trigger street violence, or if unrest becomes widely lethal.

countries.name: Sri Lanka
incidents: 20 Oct — Suwarapola, Piliyandala: Armed men in a car blocked a motorcyclist and fired several shots into the air, then fled; no injuries were reported, and police are trying to identify the suspects and motive.

11 Oct — Kalutara: The wife of the restaurant owner shot dead by motorcycle gunmen in Nagoda on 9 Oct died of her injuries in intensive care, bringing the attack's death toll to two; police had arrested the main suspect on 10 Oct.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Over the next 90 days, Sri Lanka's security situation will remain dominated by underworld and narcotics-linked shootings in the Western and Southern provinces, met by police and STF raids under the anti-drug drive, including lethal police shootouts. No indicators of insurgent, terrorist or communal conflict were observed.

regions.name: Americas
overview: Haiti's gangs have begun to target the international force directly. On 18 October an armoured vehicle carrying Salvadoran troops of the Gang Suppression Force was attacked with explosives and set on fire in Croix-des-Bouquets, helicopters sent to the scene came under fire, and four soldiers remain missing, possibly held by the Chen Mechan gang. The UN Secretary-General's report presented on 19 October counts 1,123 killed between July and early October and warns that violence is spreading into rural areas while elections remain postponed indefinitely.

Colombia's drone war continues at a pace of roughly one attack a day. On 21 October a drone attack on the police station in Pelaya (Cesar), preliminarily attributed to the ELN, wounded six officers, while in Catatumbo a soldier died of minefield injuries on 17 October and a rights observer reported at least ten bodies of armed-group members near La Gabarra (Tibu). The government claims sharp falls in homicides and attacks in Arauca, but the conflict is shifting rather than shrinking.

Criminal violence along the Andean–Pacific belt remains steady and deadly. In Ecuador, three people were shot dead outside a court in Machala on 20 October and further killings hit Guayaquil and Manabi on 19 October. In Peru, another colectivo driver was killed in Cercado de Lima on 16 October, and on 21 October the Senate approved a 60-day extension of the state of emergency in Lima and Callao from 28 October.

Political pressure is building through street mobilisation rather than violence. In Venezuela, Machado's camp marches nationwide today, 22 October, to demand a 2027 election date, while the PSUV has called a rival women's march in Caracas the same day; Washington has lifted sanctions on National Assembly president Jorge Rodriguez and keeps backing talks that exclude Machado. In Bolivia, Morales-aligned groups announced new national mobilisations on 19 October against the diesel price rise, and in Cuba blackout protests continue in Granma while prosecutors seek up to 13 years for 18 Moron protesters, six of them minors.

countries.name: Venezuela
incidents: 22 Oct — Caracas and other cities: Vente Venezuela held nationwide mobilisations, with the main rally called for Plaza Venezuela, to demand a presidential election in 2027, the release of political prisoners (322 according to Foro Penal) and Machado's safe return. No outcome had been reported at the time of writing.
19 Oct — Caracas: PSUV leader Diosdado Cabello called a chavista women's march in Caracas for 22 October, the same day as the opposition protests.

18 Oct — Caracas: The opposition Plataforma Unitaria Democratica proposed a national agreement and recognised the leadership of Machado and Edmundo Gonzalez, who are excluded from the US-backed talks with the Rodriguez government.

20 Oct — Washington/Caracas: The US lifted financial sanctions on National Assembly president Jorge Rodriguez, and President Trump said a Delcy Rodriguez–Machado election contest 'would be interesting'. No election date has been set.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. There were no armed clashes or casualties this week; the situation remains political tension with controlled protest and managed repression. Rival marches on the same day in Caracas are the main short-term flashpoint, and the reaction of police and colectivos will show whether mass opposition rallies are tolerated. US–Venezuela rapprochement, now including sanctions relief for Jorge Rodriguez, keeps the risk of external military action low but deepens the rift between Washington and the Machado camp. Over the next 90 days, expect continued pressure for an electoral timetable, incremental prisoner releases alongside short-term detentions, and a possible test if Machado attempts to return. The border states (Tachira, Apure, Zulia) remain exposed to ELN and FARC-dissident movement as Colombia's offensive continues. Upgrade to HIGH if rallies are violently dispersed with casualties, if border clashes become recurring and deadly, or if the US-backed dialogue collapses.

countries.name: Colombia
incidents: 21 Oct — Pelaya, Cesar: Explosives dropped from drones struck the police station before dawn, wounding six police officers and damaging the building. Police preliminarily blamed the ELN's Camilo Torres Restrepo Front.

21 Oct — Tibu, Norte de Santander: A human rights observer reported at least ten bodies of armed-group members at kilometre 19 of the road to La Gabarra, amid fighting between the ELN and the 33rd Front. The Office of the High Commissioner for Peace said it was verifying the reports.

17 Oct — Catatumbo, Norte de Santander: A soldier died three days after stepping on a landmine during operations against FARC dissidents; the Defence Ministry attributed the minefield to the 33rd Front of the Calarca dissidents.

21 Oct — Arauca: President De la Espriella said homicides fell 56.3% and attacks on security forces 71% between 7 August and 15 October compared with last year, and announced reinforced operations against the ELN and FARC dissidents.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. This week brought another drone attack on a police station, a fatal minefield casualty and reports of a mass-casualty clash between armed groups in Catatumbo. These fit the definition of sustained insurgency with regular deaths and territory held by armed groups.
