More than 320 drone attacks have been recorded in 2026, about one a day, with Mordisco-linked dissidents and the ELN responsible for most. Over the next 90 days, expect continued drone and explosive attacks on police stations and bases in Cauca, Valle del Cauca, Choco, Cesar and Norte de Santander, and further government bombing raids with the risk of civilian and minor casualties. Claimed security gains in Arauca may reflect displacement of armed groups toward Catatumbo and across the Venezuelan border rather than a real decline. Watch for confirmation of the Tibu death toll, the first mass-casualty urban drone attack, and the rollout of national anti-drone measures.

countries.name: Haiti
incidents: 19–21 Oct — Croix-des-Bouquets: Four Salvadoran soldiers of the Gang Suppression Force remain missing despite ground and air searches. Le Nouvelliste, citing government sources, said they may have been captured by the Chen Mechan gang; the UN demanded their immediate release.

18 Oct — Santo, Croix-des-Bouquets: Gangs attacked an armoured vehicle carrying Salvadoran GSF troops with explosives and set it on fire; helicopters sent to the scene also came under fire. AP called it the biggest attack on the force since it began operations. The area is contested by the Chen Mechan, Kraze Barye and 400 Mawozo gangs.

19 Oct — New York: The UN Secretary-General's report to the Security Council said gang violence killed 1,123 people and injured 440 between July and early October, with attacks in Saint-Michel-de-l'Atalaye, Marigot and Leogane showing spread into rural areas. The GSF had 1,563 personnel on 12 October against 5,550 authorised.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Gangs control most of Port-au-Prince and expanding rural areas, and have now mounted a coordinated attack on the international force itself, while elections remain postponed without a date. This fits loss of state control over a significant part of the territory. Over the next 90 days, expect gangs to keep testing the under-strength GSF with ambushes, kidnappings of personnel and fire on aircraft; the fate of the missing Salvadoran soldiers is a key test for contributing countries' willingness to stay. Clearance operations from the Artibonite base are likely to trigger reprisals against civilians, and violence is spreading to rural communes in the West, Artibonite and Centre. Expect further displacement beyond the current 1.5 million. Watch for a hostage or ransom scenario involving the soldiers, new troop arrivals, and any new electoral calendar.

countries.name: Cuba
incidents: 21 Oct — Moron, Ciego de Avila: Prosecutors seek 5 to 13 years in prison for sedition against 18 people, six of them minors, over the March 2026 protest in which the local Communist Party office was stormed and damaged after prolonged blackouts.
19 Oct — Nationwide: The Electric Union forecast an impact of 2,020 MW at evening peak because of a generation deficit of 1,990 MW, meaning extended blackouts across most of the island.

16–17 Oct — Santa Rita, Jiguani (Granma): Residents protested during a blackout; a police patrol that arrived failed to disperse them, according to Diario de Cuba. The report has not been independently verified.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. There is no armed conflict, but generation still covers well under half of demand and the collapse of basic services keeps producing local protests, now reaching Granma, while the state answers with heavy sedition sentences, including for minors. This fits the HIGH definition. Over the next 90 days, another nationwide grid collapse is likely given fuel shortages; each one tends to trigger pot-banging, street blockades and targeted arrests. The security apparatus remains cohesive and the tactic of restoring power to protesting areas keeps unrest local. The Moron trial could become a new grievance if long sentences are handed down to minors. Upgrade to CRITICAL only if protests coordinate across several cities, security forces use lethal force, or state control visibly erodes. Watch also for migration pressure and changes in US fuel restrictions.

countries.name: Ecuador
incidents: 20 Oct — Machala, El Oro: Three people were shot dead outside a judicial unit shortly after appearing in a hearing over an alleged kidnapping. Police later arrested two suspects.

19 Oct — Guayaquil: Two men were shot dead in the 22 de Abril cooperative on Isla Trinitaria, another fatal attack took place under the first bridge of the Via Perimetral, and a tricimoto driver was attacked on Avenida Ernesto Alban.

19 Oct — Calceta, Manabi: Former police officer Jhonny Castillo Alcivar (47), working as driver and bodyguard for a former legislative adviser, was killed with more than 25 shots near the Plaza Civica.
countries.coa: CRITICAL maintained. Contract killings continue daily in Guayaquil, Machala and Manabi, including an execution at a courthouse, by gangs the state treats as parties to an internal armed conflict. Homicides of minors are at a record level and total killings still exceed 20 a day. This meets the CRITICAL definition. The state of exception expires on 14 November and is likely to be extended or replaced by a renewed curfew. Operation Muralla against Comandos de la Frontera may trigger retaliation against security forces in Orellana and Sucumbios. Over 90 days, expect further US-supported operations against Los Lobos, Los Choneros and border groups, prison unrest, and attacks on judges, prison staff, ex-police and local officials, with courthouses emerging as a new risk point.

countries.name: Peru
incidents: 21 Oct — Lima: The Senate approved, by 54 votes to none with one abstention, a 60-day extension of the state of emergency in Lima Metropolitana and Callao from 28 October, citing crime and violence. Police keep control of internal order with armed forces support.
16 Oct — Cercado de Lima: Alejandro Temoche Valdez, a taxi driver working as a colectivo, was shot dead at night while carrying passengers. Police are investigating the motive.

16 Oct — Lima: Prosecutors said the 'Los Alcaeda' gang killed four drivers who refused to pay extortion fees and extorted at least 83 transport workers. La Republica counts more than 80 drivers killed and 160 attacks on transport in Lima and Callao in 2026.
countries.coa: HIGH maintained. Extortion networks continue to kill transport workers weekly in Lima and Callao. This is recurring deadly violence by organised criminal groups, although the state has not lost territorial control. The renewal of the state of emergency to late December keeps soldiers on the streets but has not changed the killing rate. Transport unions are cooperating with police for now, but another high-profile killing or threat letter could quickly revive strike calls. Over 90 days, expect continued weekly killings of drivers, more arrests of extortion cells, and pressure from President Fujimori's government to treat extortion gangs as terrorists. Upgrade triggers include attacks on candidates or officials, a mass-casualty extortion bombing, or violent clashes during a strike.

countries.name: Bolivia
incidents: 19 Oct — Cochabamba: Morales-aligned organisations announced new nationwide mobilisations against the government's economic measures, starting with a march in Cochabamba. They demand repeal of Decree 5716, which raised the diesel price by 163%, and Decree 5727 on restructuring or closing loss-making state companies.
countries.coa: MODERATE maintained. Opposition to the diesel price rise has moved from postponement back to announced mobilisations, but so far without blockades, clashes or casualties. This remains political tension with limited violence. The state of exception (to 17 December) and police and army checkpoints around La Paz give the government tools to deter or clear blockades, but forced clearances in Cochabamba coca-growing areas or on main highways could produce casualties quickly, as during the deadly May–June blockades. Morales, under an arrest warrant for terrorism since July, has an incentive to escalate from his Chapare stronghold. Over 90 days, watch Cochabamba, Potosi and El Alto. Return to HIGH if multi-day blockades resume, clearances cause deaths, or protests turn into calls for President Paz's resignation.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
incidents: 19 Oct — Nationwide/border: The General Directorate of Migration detained 1,549 undocumented foreigners and deported 1,240 Haitians in one day, with 292 arrests in Dajabon.
15–16 Oct — Nationwide/border: Migration authorities reported 2,278 undocumented foreigners detained in a single day, with Dajabon and Elias Pina again leading the border provinces.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. There was no organised armed or political violence this week; activity was limited to large-scale migration enforcement and routine policing. Over the next 90 days, expect deportations to continue at more than a thousand a day and border-wall construction to proceed. The 18 October gang ambush on GSF troops near Croix-des-Bouquets and spreading rural gang violence in Haiti raise the risk of new displacement toward Dajabon and Elias Pina. The Dominican Republic will remain a cocaine transit point with joint US maritime interdictions. The main risks are diplomatic and humanitarian friction with Haiti and scrutiny of police conduct, not internal instability.

countries.name: Jamaica
incidents: 20 Oct — Mandeville, Manchester: Two unidentified men were killed when police returned fire during an operation and stopped their car. INDECOM opened an investigation.

16 Oct — Sligoville, St Catherine: Gunmen ambushed a police operation, reportedly using a child in a false-surrender ploy. A police corporal and three gunmen were killed, two other officers were shot, and a 10-year-old girl was wounded. INDECOM is reviewing the incident.
countries.coa: LOW maintained. Violence remains criminal rather than organised political or armed-group violence, and murders are on course for a historic low. The Sligoville ambush, in which a corporal was killed, is a serious but isolated gang confrontation, and does not amount to recurring organised attacks on the state. The main tension remains the high rate of killings by security forces, with two more fatal police shootings in Mandeville this week. Over 90 days, expect further contested police shootings, possible retaliation against police after Sligoville, localized roadblock protests and rights criticism. Watch for any repeat of planned ambushes on police, escalation into sustained unrest in Kingston/St Andrew or St Catherine, and late-season hurricane impacts.
